title: ChatGPT Wallet lets OpenAI’s AI agents shop and check out for you
summary: OpenAI on Friday, November 13, 2026, launched ChatGPT Wallet, a feature that lets its AI agents, called dots, help users decide what to buy and then complete the purchase on their behalf, TechCrunch reported. It starts with a limited number of U.S. ChatGPT Pro subscribers, ages 18 and up, with a U.S.-issued Visa, Mastercard or American Express card. Users review the items, the total and the payment card before checkout and approve each purchase with a security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint. The wallet then charges the card with a payment token, a substitute for the real card details, so they aren’t shared with the dot or the merchant, and shoppers keep card rewards and dispute protections. OpenAI plans to let users set spending limits and pre-approve some purchases later. One hurdle: some retailers block AI agents, and the largest, Amazon, steers shoppers to its own Alexa agent. OpenAI also published a Commerce Partner Playbook for retailers.

title: Researcher finds export-banned Nvidia Blackwell ‘fingerprints’ in China’s top open AI models
summary: Leading open-weight AI models from Chinese companies appear to have been trained on Nvidia Blackwell chips that the U.S. bars from shipping to China, according to new research reported by TechCrunch on Friday, November 13, 2026. Will DePue, a former OpenAI researcher who leads the nonprofit research group Unemployment Labs, analyzed the weights of open models from DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group, and found compelling evidence that closely watched releases, including Moonshot’s Kimi K3 models and DeepSeek’s V4 models, bear fingerprints of training on Blackwell chips. TechCrunch notes that doesn’t mean the models were trained entirely on Nvidia chips or that export laws were necessarily broken, since the chips could sit in offshore data centers, such as in Malaysia. Epoch AI estimates about two million advanced chips entered China in 2024 and 2025 through schemes designed to hide their final destination. The findings add pressure on Nvidia, whose CEO Jensen Huang left this week after admitting an affair with Alice Huang, an executive of Megaspeed, a company implicated in smuggling Nvidia chips into China.

title: FAA lifts a four-hour nationwide ground stop as officials look at whether its new AI airspace system played a role
summary: The FAA halted takeoffs across the U.S. on Friday, November 13, 2026, issuing a national ground stop at 3:44 p.m. ET “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety,” then lifting it at 8:15 p.m. ET, more than four hours later, The Verge reported. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed an aging air traffic control system, saying analog telecom switches and routers “got overloaded with data,” and he and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin confirmed that “patches” to the existing system sparked the issue. Asked about a possible link to SMART (Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories), a cloud-based AI system activated nationwide on November 10, Mullin said officials were looking into it. Air Space Intelligence, which designed SMART under a 12-year, $875 million contract, denied any connection. Mullin said there was no reason to suspect a cyberattack. FlightAware listed 9,124 U.S. flights delayed and 5,901 canceled as of 8:39 p.m. ET.

title: Amazon reportedly plans a ‘World Product Graph’ indexing products sold anywhere online, for people and AI agents
summary: Amazon has plans to build a vault of data on every product sold anywhere on the internet, even items it doesn’t sell, and make it available through its own site, The Verge reported Friday, November 13, 2026, citing Reuters. The project, called the “World Product Graph,” is meant to keep shoppers from leaving Amazon to research products on Reddit or Google, and to make AI shopping agents more likely to rely on Amazon’s index. It would also feed Amazon’s AI shopping assistant, Alexa for Shopping, previously called Rufus: an internal document says “Many Rufus answers are factually wrong or incomplete,” and running searches through the AI is expensive, so more data is meant to make it more accurate and able to use cheaper models. The plan reportedly depends on discovering how brands organize products on their own websites, and the document lists an October 1, 2027 release date, though Reuters says it’s unclear if or when it will ship. Amazon told Reuters draft documents “often paint an incomplete picture.”

title: S&P 500 slips 0.4% Friday as chip stocks slide, but logs its first winning week since October
summary: The S&P 500 fell 30.73 points, or 0.40%, to 7,561.67 on Friday, November 13, 2026, and the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.91% to 25,136.27 as concerns about Nvidia pressured technology shares, while the Dow rose 0.10% to 52,347.55, Reuters reported via The Straits Times. For the week, the S&P 500 still gained 2.51% and the Nasdaq 2.27%, both snapping four-week losing streaks, and the Dow climbed 2.07%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 3.4%, and technology was the worst of the 11 major S&P sectors, down 1.7%. Nvidia slid 2% for a sixth straight weekly decline, its longest streak since October 2012. Airline shares dropped late after the FAA’s nationwide ground stop. October producer prices came in slightly cooler than expected but rose 6.5% from a year earlier, the largest annual gain since November 2022, keeping a December Fed rate hike fully priced in. Anthropic’s much-anticipated IPO comes next week.

title: AMD sinks 8.75% as Friday’s AI-chip sell-off erases its early Nvidia-turmoil gains
summary: Advanced Micro Devices closed at $534.06 on Friday, November 13, 2026, down 8.75%, as early buying in AI-chip names reversed into a sector-wide sell-off, The Motley Fool reported. Trading volume reached 48.6 million shares, about 98% above the three-month average of 24.6 million. AMD had been up as much as 30% this week on bets that turmoil at Nvidia could help its rivals, and it still ended the week with solid gains, the Fool said. Nvidia closed at $162.85, down 2.01%, and Intel finished at $59.66, down 2.52%. Last week AMD reported third-quarter revenue of $13.4 billion and said data-center sales nearly doubled from a year earlier. The Fool argued investors shouldn’t be overly concerned about Friday’s drop, which it tied to uncertainty around Nvidia in its post-Jensen Huang era. Investors are now watching Nvidia’s earnings report next week and demand for AI chips.

title: Arm slides 6.5% after a report that Nvidia’s board approached CEO Rene Haas to succeed Huang
summary: Arm Holdings shares fell 6.5% on Friday, November 13, 2026, after the Financial Times reported that Nvidia’s board had approached Arm CEO Rene Haas as a potential successor to Jensen Huang, Investing.com reported. Haas is among several candidates, and according to people cited by the FT he has not been offered the job and there is no guarantee he would accept it. Haas has led Arm since 2022, previously spent more than seven years at Nvidia, and maintains close relationships with Huang and several Nvidia board members. Investing.com said a move would raise questions about continuity at Arm, whose processor architecture is central to much of the chip industry, including Nvidia’s own Grace and Vera CPU platforms. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell around 5% on the day, with AMD and Broadcom among the notable decliners. Arm declined to comment, and Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

title: Nebius and CoreWeave slump as Huang’s exit raises fears about Nvidia-backed AI financing
summary: Nvidia-backed neocloud companies led a fresh slide in AI stocks on Friday, November 13, 2026, as investors worried about AI financing after Jensen Huang’s abrupt exit, Reuters reported via Investing.com. Nebius Group slumped 9% and CoreWeave 8.8% in midday trading, extending sharp declines from Thursday. Under Huang, Nvidia financed infrastructure built around its chips, a strategy that drove demand but raised questions about circular funding. “It’s a short-term death blow to the industry because the amount of vendor financing and financing guarantees that Nvidia and Jensen Huang stepped into are now over,” said Thomas Hayes, chairman of Great Hill Capital. Nscale, a British cloud provider also backed by Nvidia, amended its IPO filing to say it expects a $1.7 billion net loss for the nine months ended September 30, wider than $433.3 million a year earlier. “This company is pure uncertainty right now,” Interactive Brokers’ Steve Sosnick said of Nvidia, whose earnings and Anthropic’s market debut come next week.

title: Thinking Machines releases open weights for Inkling 2 Small, a 594-billion-parameter multimodal model
summary: Thinking Machines Lab has made the weights of Inkling 2 Small downloadable, completing the move from the model’s November 5 hosted-only introduction, Open Model Weights reported Friday, November 13, 2026. A November 12 update to the company’s launch article points to a new Hugging Face repository where the checkpoint is labeled Apache 2.0. Inkling 2 Small is a sparse mixture-of-experts multimodal model with 594 billion total parameters and about 17 billion active per token; its 48-layer decoder routes each token to eight of 384 experts and accepts text and images, answering in text. The model card describes up to one million tokens of context, while the launch article discussed a 256K served context. It is no laptop model: the official minimum is 500GB of combined GPU memory for the native NVFP4 checkpoint or 800GB for MXFP8, such as two B300 or four H200 GPUs. Open Model Weights notes the benchmark tables are the publisher’s own and haven’t been independently replicated.

title: G-STAR open models generate a 1024x1024 image in 2.5 seconds on a single GPU, researchers say
summary: A team from Peking University’s DAGroup, together with Meituan Longcat, SJTU and co-authors, has released G-STAR, an open framework for autoregressive image generation that produces a 1024x1024 image in 2.5 seconds on a single Nvidia H200, mlllm.io reported Saturday, November 14, 2026. The researchers say that is about 20 times faster than earlier discrete autoregressive models: 21.57 times faster than Janus-Pro-7B and 8.36 times faster than Emu3.5-34B. Weights for two models and inference code are on Hugging Face: G-STAR-Pro-8B, with 32x compression, and G-STAR-Flash-1.7B, with an effective 64x compression. Pro-8B can also edit images from text instructions, scoring 7.45 on GEdit-Bench versus 7.53 for GPT-Image-1. The approach packs more codes into each compressed position, so far fewer steps are needed per picture. mlllm.io cautions that all quality scores are author-reported and that the speed comparison is against older autoregressive models, not modern diffusion systems.

title: Pruna AI’s free adapters erase objects from photos, shadows and reflections included
summary: Pruna AI has released P-Q-Image-2.1-Remove-Object, a set of open LoRA adapters for the Qwen-Image-2.1 image model that remove an object from a photo along with its shadow and reflection without shifting the remaining pixels, mlllm.io reported Friday, November 13, 2026. Shadows and reflections are removed even outside the marked area. Three variants are free on Hugging Face: distilled versions that finish in 6 or 8 steps instead of 40 and run without classifier-free guidance, plus a 40-step base version. The fast variants stack the task adapter on top of Pruna’s distillation LoRA. Ready-made ComfyUI workflows, a custom node and an online demo in Pruna’s playground are also available. Pruna lists limitations up front: with a rough mask, the model may remove a neighboring object, and the filled area can look smoother than its surroundings, with a faint mesh-like artifact. The release includes no quantitative measurements of quality, speed or memory needs.

title: ElevenLabs previews ElevenAI, a team app for meeting notes, dictation and AI follow-ups
summary: Voice AI company ElevenLabs, valued at $22 billion, this week released ElevenAI, an experimental app that combines meeting note-taking, dictation and agent integration for teams, TechCrunch reported Friday, November 13, 2026. Launched at its 11/11 Summit in New York, ElevenAI is still in preview and requires signing up for early access. It takes notes across meetings, notifies other participants that the conversation is being recorded, lets users query information across meetings and offers live help recalling details from older conversations. Companies can connect ElevenAgent to take follow-up actions, such as drafting an email from meeting notes, and a dictation feature turns speech into cleaned-up text in any app, with support for over 90 languages. TechCrunch notes that Fireflies, Wispr Flow and Granola have all released competing features in recent months. In the last week, ElevenLabs also launched its v3 Scribe speech-to-text models, with live transcription and fine-tuning on a company’s own data.

title: Drogue raises $20 million to power floating AI data centers with the ocean’s heat
summary: Drogue, a six-month-old startup in Washington, D.C., is building a system that harvests heat from the ocean to power data centers aboard floating vessels, TechCrunch reported exclusively on Friday, November 13, 2026. The company said it has raised $20 million from investors including XYZ Venture Capital, Toyota Ventures and Slow Ventures. Its approach, ocean thermal energy conversion, draws in warm surface water to cool the servers, uses that warmed water to boil ammonia that drives a turbine, and condenses the ammonia with cold water pumped from 1,000 meters deep. Founder and CEO Sam Sipe, a former Navy E-2D Hawkeye pilot, says data centers run on 8- to 10-year real-estate timelines while “AI demand has increased 10x in just the last three years.” Drogue has designed a multi-megawatt prototype to be installed on a traditional oceangoing ship and sent to sea in early 2028. It has preliminary approval from the American Bureau of Shipping and is buying its first ship.

title: Cloudflare open-sources Kitesurf, a Chromium-free browser engine for AI agents
summary: Cloudflare has open-sourced Kitesurf, an experimental browser engine for AI agents that runs on Cloudflare Workers without Chromium or browser containers, mlllm.io reported Friday, November 13, 2026. The code is on GitHub under the Apache 2.0 license. Instead of farms of headless Chromium containers, Kitesurf assembles a rendering stack from Rust and WebAssembly components: Blitz for the DOM and layout, Stylo for CSS, Boa for JavaScript, Linebender for text and 2D graphics and Krilla for PDFs. With it, the engine parses HTML, applies CSS, runs JavaScript and renders screenshots, PDFs and HTML. It talks to outside tools through the standard Chrome DevTools Protocol, so Puppeteer or an AI agent can connect to it. It can be run locally for free, though deploying it to a Cloudflare account requires a paid Workers plan. mlllm.io notes that claims of lower automation costs haven’t been measured yet, and it is unknown how many real websites render correctly.

title: Singapore teens win Samsung’s Solve for Tomorrow with a smartwatch app that helps students with special needs through moments of distress
summary: Four students from Temasek Secondary School, Saanvi Gupta, Ayesha Nadya, Malyanah Rizwana and Sakeenah Banu, won the Grand Prize in Samsung Solve for Tomorrow 2026 in Singapore for WristAssured, a smartwatch app that helps students with special educational needs recognize and manage moments of distress, Samsung Newsroom Singapore announced Tuesday, November 10, 2026. Using a Galaxy Watch’s sensors, the app reads heart rate, heart-rate variability, sweat activity, skin temperature and movement against each student’s own baseline. When it detects stress, it checks in with gentle vibrations and calming visual prompts, and if distress persists it alerts SEN officers or teachers. “Technology should adapt to the individual rather than have the individual adapt to the technology,” Gupta said. The team won S$7,000 and S$10,000 in Samsung products. Third place went to Pei Hwa Secondary School’s SafeSignal, a wearable that helps nonspeaking autistic children signal for help in emergencies. The contest drew 116 entries.

title: A South Carolina senior becomes the youngest InnoVision winner with Pathly, an AI guide for students
summary: Grace Brusky, a senior at Cyber Academy of South Carolina, became the youngest winner in the 28-year history of the South Carolina InnoVision Awards on November 5, when her artificial intelligence platform Pathly won the Community Enrichment Award at the Thornblade Club in Greer, Hoodline reported Wednesday, November 11, 2026. Brusky co-founded Pathly with her father, Alan Brusky. The platform learns each student’s interests and strengths and builds a running roadmap across colleges, careers, courses and scholarships. It is free for students, while schools and districts use a paid version with tools to guide large numbers of students at once. Pathly’s materials cite a national counselor-to-student ratio of 372 to 1, far above the 250-to-1 the American School Counselor Association recommends. The company won a $25,000 startup grant from the South Carolina Research Authority earlier this year. Brusky, who has a 4.6 GPA and takes dual-enrollment courses through Winthrop University, is working toward a career in environmental science.

title: STEM Saturday at the Lafayette Science Museum asks: is your Thanksgiving turkey a dinosaur?
summary: Is the turkey on your Thanksgiving table actually a dinosaur? The University of Louisiana at Lafayette Science Museum, 433 Jefferson St., hosts STEM Saturday today, Saturday, November 14, from 10 a.m. to 1:30 p.m., exploring the paleontology fact that birds are living dinosaurs, according to the museum’s event page. Young scientists will investigate what turkeys and dinosaurs have in common, test different “dinosaur beaks” to see which collect food best and create their own Thanksgiving dinosaur, using clues from bones, feet, feathers and eggs. Activities are open-ended, so visitors can come and go while touring the exhibits and planetarium, and they’re included with regular museum admission. The program is geared to elementary and middle school ages, but all ages are welcome. STEM Saturdays are made possible by a grant from Halliburton. The museum is open until 6 p.m. on Saturdays and suggests following its Facebook page for updates on new and cancelled events.

title: LHSAA State Volleyball Championships wrap up at the Cajundome today
summary: The LHSAA State Volleyball Championships conclude today, Saturday, November 14, at the Cajundome, 444 Cajundome Blvd., according to the arena’s event page. Doors open at 8 a.m., and play is listed from 9 a.m. Saturday’s schedule includes Westminster Christian vs. Episcopal of Acadiana, Metairie Park Country Day vs. Dunham on Center Court, University Lab vs. Archbishop Hannan and St. Thomas More vs. a team to be determined, with sessions listed into the evening at 7 p.m. Only single-day tickets are sold; the box office opens one hour before the first game of the day, and there is no re-entry. Children under 2 get in free on a parent’s lap. A clear-bag policy is in effect, and the Cajundome is cashless, accepting cards and tap-to-pay. Can’t make it? All rounds are broadcast live on the NFHS Network. General parking is at the Cajundome, with overflow parking across the street.

title: The Acadiana Heart Walk steps off at Moncus Park this afternoon
summary: The American Heart Association’s Acadiana Heart Walk comes to Moncus Park today, Saturday, November 14, according to the park’s event listing. The event opens at 3 p.m., and the walk begins at 4:15 p.m., with 5K and Survivor Mile route options. Registration is open through the American Heart Association, which produces the event. By joining Heart Walk, participants become part of more than a million people in over 300 cities across America taking a stand against heart disease and helping save lives, the listing says.

title: Ordinary World brings ’80s new wave to Rock’n’Bowl de Lafayette tonight
summary: Rock’n’Bowl de Lafayette, 905 Jefferson St., hosts Ordinary World tonight, Saturday, November 14, at 9 p.m., according to the venue’s event page, which bills the night as ’80s New Wave. Cover is listed at $17 plus a $0.43 ticket service fee, and card fees are added to the cover charge. The cover does not include bowling, so bring extra if you plan to roll a few frames between songs. Anyone under 18 must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian. It’s a late-night option for capping off a busy Saturday with a dose of ’80s new wave.

title: Girls on the Run 5K brings a medal for every finisher to Moncus Park Sunday
summary: The Girls on the Run 5K comes to Moncus Park on Sunday, November 15, according to the park’s event listing. Inspiration Village opens at 12:45 p.m., and the 5K begins at 2 p.m. The event is non-competitive, and men, women, boys and girls of all ages are invited. Every finisher receives a custom Girls on the Run 5K medal, a shirt and post-race food, and packet pickup for shirts and bib numbers is available on race day at the information table. Registration is open. Girls on the Run says it inspires people of all abilities to build self-confidence, with volunteer coaches leading lessons that blend physical activity with life skills like managing emotions, fostering friendships and expressing empathy. At the end of each season, teams complete a community impact project and run a 5K together.

title: Rusty Metoyer brings zydeco to Rock’n’Bowl de Lafayette Sunday evening
summary: Zydeco musician Rusty Metoyer plays Rock’n’Bowl de Lafayette, 905 Jefferson St., on Sunday, November 15, at 5 p.m., according to the venue’s event page, which lists the act as a zydeco band. Tickets are listed at $17 plus a $0.43 ticket service fee. Anyone under 18 must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian. The early-evening start makes it an easy way to close out the weekend with live Creole music before the workweek begins.
